flags.text: Difficulty: the bank marks this d 3, but doubling 23 is far below DAT QR level, and all four distractors are arithmetic slips (ten light, ten over, tens only, an extra hundred) with no concept behind them. Thomas may want a real setup item in its place.
The bank why "(20 + 3) x 2 = 40 + 6" never states 46; the explainer supplies the last step.

routing: Needs a route: the view opens from data-go="mental"; its two number boxes need a state reader. The skill page opens with a Try first question on a 5-minute clock that can be skipped, and the page also holds a timed simulator elsewhere; the visual itself is untimed.

every served choice (5) has a note; one key
copy rules: ASCII, no dashes, no banned words, no letters, no competitor names, no timer or score words, budgets (explainer and visual text)
step 1 opens with a move: "Read the"

arithmetic in the text holds: 4 claims (23 + 23 = 46; 20 x 2 = 40; 3 x 2 = 6; 40 + 6 = 46)

changes: Re-review fix: a third step checks the size (each leg a little over 20 km, so the round trip is a little over 40 and under 50; 46 fits). It was the only G1 sidecar with fewer than 3 steps
Re-review suggestion taken: the 56 note says "a phantom carry" (was "a carrying slip", which the next sentence contradicted: 23 + 23 needs no carry)

served.stem: A commute is 23 kilometers each way. How many kilometers is the round trip?

answer.line: A round trip is there and back: 23 + 23 = 46 km.

steps: Read the words before the numbers. Round trip means there and back: two legs of 23 km.
Double it in pieces: 20 x 2 = 40 and 3 x 2 = 6, so 40 + 6 = 46 km.
Check the size: each leg is a little over 20 km, so the round trip is a little over 40 and under 50. 46 fits.

choices.note: 36 is ten short of 46, a slip in the adding with no rule behind it. 40 + 6 = 46.
40 doubles the 20 and leaves out 3 x 2. Add the 6: 46.
56 is ten past 46, a phantom carry. 23 + 23 needs no carry at all.
146 adds a hundred that is not there. Two legs of 23 km stay under 50.

visual.alt: Top bar: two 23 km legs end to end, there and back. The bottom bar, the same length and outlined, is the 46 km round trip. A dashed mark at 40 shows where doubling only the tens stops.
visual.caption: Lay the two legs end to end: the round trip bar matches them exactly.
